Alternate and Variant Rules.name: Alternate and Variant Rules
Alternate and Variant Rules.text:
Alternate Rules

The following alternate rules are suggestions for GMs who want to change their games to emphasize the characters growth differently.

Lore Driven Backgrounds

Since backgrounds often help conceptualize the starting point for many characters, lore skill feats can further accentuate the role of the characters background within their past. For a more lore driven background, characters that take backgrounds that grant a Lore skill and a skill feat can choose to replace the granted skill feat with a 1st-level Lore skill feat that requires being trained in that lore skill.

Journey Learning

Over the course of a character's adventuring, they will learn about the world around them, sometimes adapting that knowledge through the lens of the past and sometimes in adapting new knowledge. While the Lore characters gain through their background often represents their history, it might make sense for the journey forward to also foster their previous life. If you are using the Journey Learning alternate rules, characters gain a skill increase to a Lore skill they have access to at 3rd, 7th, and 15th level.

Can I Keep 'Em?

The guides for pets include an override for GMs to allow other familiar abilities, such as allowing a parrot to gain speech or a monkey to gain manual dexterity, but not some pets might not be animals and adventurers could encounter other creatures that make good pets. GMs might allow adventurers with @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-feats-plus.player-options.Item.WMU1TttHoFmFx2ug]{Mature Pet} to select creatures that would normally have one of the following abilities: construct, dragon, elemental, fungus, ooze (Witches+), plant, or undead in addition to any subsequent familiar abilities that would normally require those abilities.

Skill Issue

While additional skill increases can help expand character roles, rogues or investigators already have a lot of skill increases. Though @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-feats-plus.player-options.Item.3sbZtKdfHKQq91N2]{Skill Expertise} may not cause issues, it could allow these characters to encroach on roles of their peers. To combat this, it might make sense to limit characters to taking Skill Expertise once per 2-4 levels, to keep party roles defined. Alternatively, you could remove the skill trait, allowing the feat to only be taken with general feats.

Variant Rules

The following rules are alternate rules sets for granting feats, particularly with respect to the free archetype rule variant.

The Basic Pack and The Unrestricted Plus Pack can be enabled in the Feats+ module settings. To use these settings you must enable the Pathfinder 2nd edition's Campaign Feats section in the Pathfinder Second Edition settings under the Campaign tab in Manage Homebrew Elements. Once you enable the campign feats section and select the variant rule you wish to use you will need to refresh to display the additional feat slots on the actor's feats and features tab.

The Basic Pack

At 1st level your character gains an additional 1st-level class feat and an additional general feat. At 2nd level, your character gains an additional 2nd-level class feat. Your 2nd-level class feat does not have to be an archetype feat but you must still meet any other requirements of your selection.

The Natural Pack

All ancestries gain access to the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.heritages.Item.hFBwsVcSnNCJoimo] heritage and the natural ambition human feat in addition to their normal feats. Humans can choose one ancestry other than their own instead of gaining a heritage. They gain access to that ancestries' feats 1st-level feats in addition to their own feats.

The Seasoned Pack

All ancestries gain access to the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.heritages.Item.Nd9hdX8rdYyRozw8] heritage and the feat restrictions for taking feats from other archetypes does not apply to the archetype you gained from the heritage. Elves can choose one ancestry other than their own instead of gaining a heritage. They do not gain a 1st-level elf feat but instead gain a heritage from the ancestry they chose.

The Unrestricted Plus Pack

At 1st level your character gains an additional 1st-level class feat and an additional general feat. At 2nd level and every two levels thereafter,your character gains an additional ancestry or class feat, chosen at the time you gain the feat. Your class feat selections do not have to be archetype feats. You must still meet any other requirements of your selections.

Nothing's Free

A large number of Pathfinder players and GMs use the free archetype variant rule in their games. Some use it verbatim, to introduce a shared commonality between all player characters, with an archetype that has enough feats at the appropriate levels, but the variant called "unrestricted free archetype" is common, where players may pick any archetype of their choosing.

This can lead to larger power differentials between characters incentivizing strength while others are incentivized by flavor, and sometimes both. It's not uncommon for players to pick "meta" options, on purpose or by accident. These large power differentials can lead to players feeling less impactful in encounters than their counterparts, leading to less fun at the table overall.

Archetypes were designed to require significant but sometimes finite investments, which can result in scenarios where the player does not have archetype feat options they believe fit their character concept either by the restriction of needing two feats from an archetype or because the concept simply doesn't require an archetype to function.

Oh The Humanity!

Players that prefer free archetype but play in games that do not use the variant rule are often drawn to the human ancestry for its ability to gain access to options not offered otherwise. The versatile human heritage with natural ambition being a common method to start the game with two additional feats. This can lead to homogenous character development.

Another ancestry option that can end up fulfilling this role is the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.heritages.Item.Nd9hdX8rdYyRozw8] heritage elf, granting a multiclass dedication at 1st level in addition to access to their ancestry feat. In both these cases, the ancestry itself is a concept enabler for some options, which can feel restricting to players. The booster pack feats variant rule seeks to alleviate these tough mechanical vs. flavor choices that often occur in the early game.

Suggested Changes.name: Suggested Changes
Suggested Changes.text:
The following are suggested changes to existing general and skill feats.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-feats-plus.player-options.Item.T1eqhmUdY3cAHvO3]{No Cause For Alarm}

Reduce the number of actions from 3 to 2 and add the following after the second sentence: "If you are a master in Diplomacy, the emanation increases to a @Template[type:emanation|distance:15], and if you are legendary in Diplomacy, increase the emanation to a @Template[type:emanation|distance:20]."

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-feats-plus.player-options.Item.1w0KXZyBzVmK2p6J]{A Home In Every Port}

Reduce the level of the general feat to level 1 and reduce the prerequisite for Charisma to a +2 modifier.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-feats-plus.player-options.Item.8ygghL7sgytX60XI]{Armor Assist}

Add the following text after the first paragraph: "In addition, when you don armor, you can attempt an Athletics or Warfare Lore check with a DC determined by the GM (but usually 15 for common armor, DC 20 for uncommon armor, and DC 25 for rare armor). If you succeed at your check, your armor gains the comfort trait until you remove your armor or 1 day has passed. After 1 day, you must remove your armor for at least 1 hour before donning your armor again to alleviate any discomfort from wearing your armor for too long."

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e-feats-plus.player-options.Item.s0PmEHLYRNzACi2K]{Influence Nature}

Add the following paragraph: "While you are near the location where you influenced nature successfully, you are considered to have taken the action to prepare to Aid for an action that creatures or the environment would be able to Aid you in (subject to GM discretion). You use Nature for your check to Aid when you call upon nature in this way. After you call upon Aid in this way, you cannot do so again for 10 minutes."

Introduction.name: Introduction
Introduction.text:
The very fabric of the game is built upon feats, so the team had to work hard to weave carefully to bolster the game and not over-complicate it as a result of those efforts. Unlike class feats which have a rather simple definition in terms of power and application, feats that all characters can use require a much more delicate approach. Not only that, but the power budgets of different feats vary quite a bit, and when comparing the strength of options that compete for both narrative and combat, you have to ensure that what's being added doesn't invalidate concepts, but instead accentuates diversity of characters. On this front, I think the Core+ team triumphed. The playtest window for this book was also incredibly long, even overlapping with other books on our production cycle. The herculean efforts that go into making a Core+ book often challenge us, Archetypes+ certainly did as well, but Feats+ was nothing short of a literal feat. We hope these new options diversify your character concepts and bring you joy.

Feats+

How we grow as characters, how we develop particular skills, our history, our future, our mysteries, and our legends. A feat is so fundamental to the idea of being heroic, that it is inescapable from all aspects of the game, whether it be a fearsome combat, a courtroom debate, a fanciful royal ball, or the reeling sense of loss from a dreadful outcome. These feats represent the heroics of adventurers however they choose to employ, endure, and exemplify them in their story. A feat is but a measure of what an adventurer is willing to do to achieve victory, the act being merely the vessel by which they breath life into the reality.

New Traits.name: New Traits
New Traits.text:
Feats+ introduces three new traits: Teamwork, triumph, and bold.

Teamwork

Teamwork

A teamwork action is a general combat strategy that you employ by using an action with the teamwork trait and designating a willing ally that meets the requirements as your partner. A teamwork lasts until you or your partner are knocked out, until its requirements (if any) are violated, until the encounter ends, or until you or your ally engage in another teamwork, whichever comes first. After you take an action with the teamwork trait, you and your partner can't take another one for 1 round. You can employ teamwork only in encounter mode. You or your partner can Dismiss a teamwork.

The Dream Works

Teamwork is often a function of actual play in general, as team members will cooperate with various activities such as Aid, flanking, buffing, or debuffing. Teamwork feats mean to simulate the idea of two characters putting their focus on each other specifically to enhance their partner, not unlike the Sniping Duo Archetype. It is appropriate to say that Sniping Duo encapsulates similar behavior as the Teamwork feats and it may be appropriate to limit their interaction with archetypes that resemble Sniping Duo or similar mechanics.

Triumph and Bold

Triumph

A triumph celebrates your acts during an encounter that make you feel triumphant and empower you to be bold. A triumph grants you benefits and gives you access to a bold action or activity. You celebrate a triumph until you get knocked out, until the encounter ends, until you use a triumph action again or until you've resolved a bold action or activity, whichever comes first. You can only celebrate a triumph while in encounter mode.

Bold

Bold actions are actions granted to you while under a triumph effect, and using an action with the bold trait ends the triumph effect after the action is resolved. You cannot use more than one bold action per turn. Once a bold action is used, you cannot gain another triumph effect for 1 round.
